correctness.summary: Claims to return the k-th lexicographically-smallest substring but instead enumerates substrings ordered by (length, start index) and counts every occurrence with multiplicity (duplicates not removed). Both the ordering and the de-duplication are wrong for a lexicographic-k query.
correctness.triggeringInput: text="ba" (bytes {'b','a'}), textLen=2, k=1. The loop yields len=1/start=0 -> "b" as count 1, so it returns "b". The 1st lexicographically-smallest distinct substring is "a" (sorted distinct: "a","b","ba"). Wrong result. For text="aa", k=2 it returns the second occurrence of "a" again rather than the next distinct substring "aa".
correctness.rootCause: Enumeration is length-major / start-major, not lexicographic; and identical substrings at different start positions are counted multiple times.
correctness.suggestedFix: Build a suffix automaton and descend transitions in ascending char order counting distinct substrings (CountSubstrings-style), or enumerate distinct substrings and sort lexicographically before indexing by k.

perf.summary: Brute-force enumerates all O(n^2) substrings counting duplicates; defeats the entire point of having a suffix automaton in this module.
perf.currentCost: Double loop over (len, start) counts every substring occurrence including duplicates up to k, O(n^2) work and counting with multiplicity rather than distinct substrings. For the k-th DISTINCT substring this is also semantically different from an automaton-based answer.
perf.proposedChange: If the goal is the k-th lexicographically-smallest DISTINCT substring, walk the suffix automaton transitions in ascending character order using the per-state distinct-substring counts (the same dp[] count machinery in KthSubstring), emitting characters greedily — O(answer length * sigma) instead of O(n^2). If duplicates are intentionally counted, at minimum break out of the outer len loop early once count would exceed achievable totals, and reuse the automaton rather than the raw text.
perf.rationale: Automaton-driven k-th-substring is linear in the output length, not quadratic in input length; it also dedups naturally. This both fixes asymptotics and aligns the function with the module's data structure.
perf.risk: Distinct-vs-multiplicity is an observable semantic choice: the current code counts WITH multiplicity, an automaton counts DISTINCT. Switching changes outputs, so confirm intended definition before replacing. If multiplicity is required as-is, only the early-exit micro-opts apply (behavior-preserving).
